clue.text: Tax for work you are obliged to do

definitions.meaning: a levy charged by the state, as on imported goods

definitions.text: work you are obliged to do
definitions.meaning: a task one is bound to carry out

explanation.definitionFit: Customs levies are so called, as is any obligation or chore you are bound to perform.

clue.text: Standing in for Pavarotti initially I sing duet poorly

indicators.note: poorly says the letters are performed badly, jumbled into a new order
initially picks out only the opening letter of the singer's surname

explanation.surface: Pavarotti's understudy makes a poor fist of the duet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives P from Pavarotti; 'poorly' scrambles P with ISINGDUET.
explanation.definitionFit: To deputise is to act as a substitute for someone else.

clue.text: Coach a few of them

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to instruct or prepare someone
a string of railway coaches makes up one of these

explanation.definitionFit: To coach is to tutor someone, and a railway string of carriages consists of several coaches coupled together.

clue.text: Not looking good from pie and horrible decaf

parts.note: a pasty is a pastry case filled with meat and vegetables, a Cornish favourite

indicators.note: horrible suggests the coffee's letters are mangled into a mess

explanation.surface: Someone looks unwell after a pie and some nasty decaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' rearranges DECAF into FACED. A pasty is a British baked pastry pie.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pale and unhealthy in complexion means one is not looking well.

clue.text: Some local cop opens drink young people like

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A local policeman opens an investigation into a drink popular with teenagers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals a run of letters lying across loc-AL COP OP-ens.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet, fruity bottled spirits mixers are marketed largely at teenagers and young adults.

clue.text: Oral examination allowed about city

indicators.note: about means the combined words turn around and are read from the end

parts.note: a viva is a spoken exam, usually defending a thesis
let means permitted

explanation.surface: A student is permitted to sit an oral exam on a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns VIVALET back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Israel's second-largest urban centre, on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Puny fellow goes to bar

parts.note: a rail is a horizontal bar

explanation.surface: A weakling goes off to the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone weak and lacking strength.

clue.text: Plant featured in art museum up in south American country

indicators.note: featured in says the turned-up gallery name appears within the country's name

parts.note: Chile is a country in South America

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters run upwards, back to front

parts.note: MoMA is New York's Museum of Modern Art

explanation.surface: A plant appears in an exhibition in a South American gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses the museum, which is then 'featured in' the country. MoMA is New York's Museum of Modern Art.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy-like herb whose flowers are used for tea.

clue.text: Lacking intellectual acuity elephant loses duck

indicators.note: loses means the zero-shaped letter is dropped from the elephant's name

parts.note: Dumbo is the flying elephant of Disney's film
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A slow-witted elephant gets rid of a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word means stupid, slow on the uptake.

clue.text: Purist left poster lying around

indicators.note: lying around says the poster word surrounds the letter for left

parts.note: a sticker is an adhesive notice or label

explanation.surface: A perfectionist complains about a leftover poster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying around' puts L inside STICKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who insists on exact correctness in every detail, much like a pedant.

clue.text: Start to read first part of play and chapter in china — that's sensible

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the friend

parts.note: china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, so a pal

indicators.note: Start to takes just the opening letter of read

parts.note: Act I is the opening section of a play

explanation.surface: Reading the opening of a play in porcelain seems a sensible plan.
explanation.walkthrough: R, ACT I and C go 'in' PAL. China is a pal from Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate).
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone level-headed, realistic and useful.

clue.text: Scare a liberal member

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A Liberal MP frightens people.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean a sudden fright or panic.

clue.text: Back in bed without medicine

indicators.note: Back means the combined letters are read in reverse
without in its old sense of outside, so the bed goes round the other word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Someone is back in bed without their medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the bed encloses the other word; 'Back' then reverses the whole, giving CINOT turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A restorative drink or medicine taken to invigorate.

clue.text: Mostly timid and one with pride in the marquee

indicators.note: Mostly says the last letter of the timid word is dropped

parts.note: pavid is a rare word for fearful or timid
a group of lions is a pride

explanation.surface: A nervous person and a proud one sit in the tent.
explanation.walkthrough: PAVID is a rare word for timid; 'Mostly' drops its D. A pride is a group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tent at a fete or sporting event can be called a marquee.

clue.text: What many people are buying? Trees to decorate with bells

indicators.note: to decorate suggests the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Christmas trees hung with bells are what everyone buys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to decorate' mixes up TREES and BELLS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit book or product is one that sells in large numbers.

clue.text: Shapely dish in gown going around western state

indicators.note: going around says the garment surrounds the state

parts.note: a slop is a loose outer garment
Cal is short for California, in the western US

explanation.surface: A woman in a gown visits a western state with a nice dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going around' has the garment enclose the state. 'Shapely dish' plays on a small dish shaped like a mollusc shell; a slop is an old word for a loose smock.
explanation.definitionFit: A shell-shaped dish for serving food is named after the mollusc's fanned shell.

clue.text: Perhaps a soldier takes lorry around cold region — bitterly cold

parts.note: a soldier is a caste of ant, so this is an example

indicators.note: around means the lorry goes around the letter for cold

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A soldier drives a lorry through a freezing landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts C inside ARTIC. An artic is a British articulated lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Pole's continent is the coldest place on Earth.

clue.text: Being foxy liven up dancing

indicators.note: dancing suggests the letters jump about into a new order

explanation.surface: Being foxy livens up the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges LIVENUP.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin-derived adjective means of or like a fox, hence cunning.

clue.text: 27 is left around toilets

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved round into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 27 across is a word for cave

explanation.surface: A cave is left lying around the toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: The '27' refers to the answer at 27 across, a word for cave; 'around' is the anagram signal, mixing that word with 'is' and the letter for left.
explanation.definitionFit: These are communal privies, as dug at a military camp.

clue.text: A white key is not artificial

definitions.meaning: a piano's white keys play the unaltered notes, neither sharp nor flat

explanation.definitionFit: On a piano the white keys play unsharpened notes, and something real rather than man-made is called that too.

clue.text: In which to stretch the French man about to be married

parts.note: le is a French word for the
a bridegroom is about to wed

explanation.surface: A Frenchman about to marry needs room to stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Room for your legs in a car or plane seat.

clue.text: You must be this in the doctor's waiting room!

definitions.text: You must be this in the doctor's waiting room!

parts.words: You must be this in the doctor's waiting room!
parts.note: a pun: the person waiting is a medical case, and waiting calmly is a virtue

explanation.definitionFit: A medical case at the doctor's surgery has to wait without complaint.

clue.text: I take part in cockney's feet exercises

indicators.note: take part in says the letter goes into the middle of the feet word

parts.note: plates of meat is Cockney rhyming slang for feet, shortened to plates

explanation.surface: Someone joins in a Londoner's foot exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take part in' puts I inside PLATES. In Cockney rhyming slang plates of meat means feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of controlled body-conditioning movements named after its German inventor, Joseph.

clue.text: Lavish glutton entertains pole at a lake

indicators.note: entertains means the greedy eater holds the pole inside

parts.note: a pig is a greedy eater
a rod is a pole, also an old unit of length

explanation.surface: A glutton hosts a Pole for a feast by the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertains' has the greedy animal play host to the pole; a rod is also an old measure of length, the pole or perch.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wastefully extravagant with money, like the son in the parable.

clue.text: Miserable and expensive — that's about right!

indicators.note: about says the costly word goes round the letter

parts.note: dear means costly

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a dreary item is expensive, and rightly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside DEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary word for dull and gloomy, a shortening of dreary.

clue.text: Hint of spark from unique fireplace

indicators.note: from here means taken away from the word for unique

parts.note: single means one of a kind

indicators.note: Hint of takes just the first letter of spark

explanation.surface: A hint of a spark comes from a one-off fireplace.
explanation.walkthrough: S, the first letter of spark, is taken 'from' SINGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for a hearth, kept alive in the cosy nook beside the fire.

clue.text: Something to drink from? Good girl!

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl, from the north of England

explanation.surface: Someone praises a girl and raises a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler or wine vessel is a drinking vessel.

clue.text: Prince Harry left large room

parts.note: Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: Prince Harry has left the large room.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Prince Hal (Henry IV plays) is the future Henry V, called Harry.
explanation.definitionFit: A large room for gatherings, banquets or concerts.

clue.text: Rent a funny cave

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Renting a cave would be a funny thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges RENTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for a cavern, used by Shakespeare in Othello.

clue.text: Where a hammer might go without delay

definitions.meaning: a hammer strikes the head of a tack

explanation.definitionFit: A hammer strikes a tack's head, and paying at once is the idiom for paying immediately.

clue.text: Suffering with cholera my son is showing sorrow

indicators.note: Suffering suggests the letters are tortured into a new shape

explanation.surface: A mother weeps over her son suffering from cholera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffering' rearranges CHOLERA, MY and S.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means tearful or inclined to weep, from Latin for tears.

clue.text: Follower of Haile Selassie returned without a Russian ruler

indicators.note: returned means what is left is read backwards
without means the letter a is taken out

parts.note: a Rastafarian, Rasta for short, venerates the Ethiopian emperor

explanation.surface: A Rastafarian goes back to Russia without a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops the final A from RASTA to give RAST, and 'returned' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor of Russia before 1917 was its tsar.
